posts.title: A Composable Thermal Solver For Heterogeneous 2.5D/3D-IC Packages (Cadence, Notre Dame)
posts.summary:
Researchers at Cadence Design Systems and the University of Notre Dame published “A Composable AI-Accelerated Iterative Solver for 3D-IC Thermal Modeling.” Abstract: “Accurate thermal analysis of heterogeneous 2.5D/3D-IC packages is essential yet computationally prohibitive. A single full-package FEM simulation can take hours, while AI-based surrogates treat the entire stack as a monolithic prediction target and... » read more
The post A Composable Thermal Solver For Heterogeneous 2.5D/3D-IC Packages (Cadence, Notre Dame) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Cadence and Notre Dame researchers introduced DAIST, an AI-accelerated thermal solver that decomposes complex 3D-IC packages into modular subdomains.
The tool achieves up to 178x speedup compared to traditional Finite Element Method (FEM) solvers while maintaining high accuracy with mean temperature errors below 0.4%.
Unlike monolithic AI models, DAIST allows for cross-topology reuse of block-level neural operators, significantly reducing the need for retraining when package designs change.

posts.title: Nanoelectromechanical Switches Target More Efficient Embedded DRAM (UC Berkeley, Samsung, Intel)
posts.summary:
Researchers at the UC Berkeley, Samsung Electronics, and Intel published “Nanoelectromechanically Gated Gain Cell eDRAM.” Abstract Excerpt: “The memory wall and the slowdown of static random access memory (SRAM) scaling have renewed interest in gain-cell embedded dynamic random access memory (DRAM). While gain cells offer high density and energy efficiency, they suffer from limited retention,... » read more
The post Nanoelectromechanical Switches Target More Efficient Embedded DRAM (UC Berkeley, Samsung, Intel) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers from UC Berkeley, Samsung, and Intel have developed a nanoelectromechanically gated gain cell to address the scaling limitations of traditional SRAM.
The design aims to overcome critical eDRAM bottlenecks, specifically limited data retention, parasitic coupling, and the requirement for high write voltages.
This innovation represents a potential pathway to maintain high-density memory performance as traditional SRAM scaling continues to slow down.

posts.title: Thermal Side Channels Create New Security Risks For Autonomous Vehicles (Missouri S&T)
posts.summary:
Researchers at Missouri University of Science and Technology published “Can Autonomous Vehicles Keep Their Cool? A Survey of Thermal Side-Channel and Perception Attacks.” Abstract excerpt: “This survey systematizes thirteen representative works into thermal perception integrity, telemetry leakage, and model-information extraction, comparing them by privilege, timescale, co-tenancy, deployability, and AV relevance. We distinguish attack family from... » read more
The post Thermal Side Channels Create New Security Risks For Autonomous Vehicles (Missouri S&T) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: A new survey from Missouri S&T highlights how thermal side-channel attacks can compromise the integrity of autonomous vehicle (AV) perception systems.
The research categorizes threats into three primary vectors: thermal perception integrity, telemetry leakage, and the extraction of sensitive model information.
As AI workloads increase thermal stress on automotive sensors, the study emphasizes the urgent need for new security defenses that operate within existing thermal management constraints.

posts.title: VW steps up China EREV push with ID. ERA 8X launch; ID. ERA 5X to follow in November
posts.summary:
The 5-seat ID. ERA 8X starts at a limited-time price of 206,800 yuan ($30,720) and is the third model in SAIC Volkswagen's ID. ERA lineup.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: SAIC Volkswagen has launched the ID. ERA 8X, an extended-range SUV priced aggressively between 206,800 and 269,800 yuan to compete with Li Auto and Aito.
The 8X is the second EREV in the ID. ERA lineup and features an 800-volt architecture, offering a combined range of up to 1,602 km.
All variants come equipped with Momenta's R7 driver-assistance system, which utilizes 192-channel LiDAR for advanced navigation on autopilot.
The company plans to further expand the lineup with the launch of the ID. ERA 5X, the first battery-electric model in the series, in November.

posts.title: Leapmotor launches A10s with LiDAR for about $13,800
posts.summary:
The A10s focuses on exclusive styling and comfort upgrades, with a CLTC range of 505 km.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Leapmotor has launched the A10s, a new variant of its small electric SUV priced at 92,800 yuan ($13,810), positioning it as a premium-styled option within the existing A10 lineup.

The vehicle maintains core performance specs from the A10 505 LiDAR variant, including a 505 km CLTC range, a 90 kW motor, and advanced driver-assistance hardware powered by Qualcomm SA8295 and SA8650 chips.
The launch serves as a strategic year-end sales push following a 24.08% month-on-month decline in A10 deliveries during September, which totaled 24,457 units.
Despite the recent dip, the A10 remains a critical volume driver for Leapmotor, accounting for over 23% of the company's record-breaking 105,656 global deliveries in September.
